manifest.title: Synthetic Product Growth: Scale the winners, fix Paid Search
manifest.description: A hands-on Data Analytics learning lab built from synthetic product-growth data.

query.description: Aggregate the synthetic channel rows into weekly funnel, revenue, and support metrics.
query.sql:
SELECT
  week_start,
  SUM(signups) AS signups,
  SUM(activated_users) AS activated_users,
  ROUND(1.0 * SUM(activated_users) / SUM(signups), 4) AS activation_rate,
  SUM(paid_conversions) AS paid_conversions,
  ROUND(1.0 * SUM(paid_conversions) / SUM(signups), 4) AS signup_to_paid_rate,
  SUM(revenue_usd) AS revenue_usd,
  SUM(support_tickets) AS support_tickets,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(support_tickets) / SUM(signups), 2) AS tickets_per_100_signups
FROM product_growth
GROUP BY week_start
ORDER BY week_start
metric_definitions: Activation rate = activated users / signups for each week.
Signup-to-paid rate = paid conversions / signups for each week.
Tickets per 100 signups = 100 × support tickets / signups for each week.
Revenue is the sum of revenue_usd in USD for each complete week.

query.description: Compare first and last complete weeks for each acquisition channel.
query.sql:
WITH channel_baselines AS (
  SELECT
    acquisition_channel,
    MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MIN(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN signups END) AS first_signups,
    MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN signups END) AS last_signups,
    1.0 * MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MIN(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN activated_users END)
      / MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MIN(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN signups END) AS first_activation_rate,
    1.0 * MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN activated_users END)
      / MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN signups END) AS last_activation_rate,
    1.0 * MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MIN(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN paid_conversions END)
      / MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MIN(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN signups END) AS first_paid_rate,
    1.0 * MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN paid_conversions END)
      / MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN signups END) AS last_paid_rate,
    MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MIN(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN revenue_usd END) AS first_revenue,
    MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN revenue_usd END) AS last_revenue,
    MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MIN(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN support_tickets END) AS first_tickets,
    MAX(CASE WHEN week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM product_growth)
      THEN support_tickets END) AS last_tickets
  FROM product_growth
  GROUP BY acquisition_channel
)
SELECT
  acquisition_channel,
  first_signups,
  last_signups,
  ROUND(1.0 * last_signups / first_signups - 1, 4) AS signup_growth,
  ROUND(first_activation_rate, 4) AS first_activation_rate,
  ROUND(last_activation_rate, 4) AS last_activation_rate,
  ROUND(last_activation_rate - first_activation_rate, 4) AS activation_rate_change,
  ROUND(100.0 * (last_activation_rate - first_activation_rate), 2) AS activation_rate_change_pp,
  ROUND(first_paid_rate, 4) AS first_paid_rate,
  ROUND(last_paid_rate, 4) AS last_paid_rate,
  ROUND(last_paid_rate - first_paid_rate, 4) AS paid_rate_change,
  ROUND(100.0 * (last_paid_rate - first_paid_rate), 2) AS paid_rate_change_pp,
  first_revenue,
  last_revenue,
  ROUND(1.0 * last_revenue / first_revenue - 1, 4) AS revenue_growth,
  first_tickets,
  last_tickets,
  ROUND(1.0 * last_tickets / first_tickets - 1, 4) AS ticket_growth
FROM channel_baselines
ORDER BY revenue_growth DESC
metric_definitions: Revenue growth = last-week revenue / first-week revenue − 1.
Activation-rate change = last-week activation rate − first-week activation rate.
Paid-rate change = last-week paid conversions/signups − first-week paid conversions/signups.
Ticket growth = last-week support tickets / first-week support tickets − 1.

blocks.body: # Synthetic Product Growth: Scale the winners, fix Paid Search

## Executive Summary

- **Top-line growth is strong.** Weekly signups increased **38.0%** and revenue increased **31.8%** from April 6 to May 25.
- **Funnel quality is weakening.** Overall activation fell **3.7 percentage points**, even as acquisition volume increased.
- **Paid Search is the clear drag.** Its activation rate fell **17.3 percentage points**, revenue declined **18.3%**, and support tickets rose **160%**.
- **Recommended action:** protect the healthy Organic base, test more investment in Partners and Referral, and pause incremental Paid Search scaling until traffic quality and onboarding are diagnosed.

## Volume is rising while funnel quality is slipping

Signups increased every week, but activation peaked at **62.7%** on April 27 and fell to **57.5%** by May 25. Support intensity moved the other way, rising from **7.41** to **9.19 tickets per 100 signups**. The growth is real, but the business is acquiring progressively more users who need help or do not reach activation.

## Paid Search is the drag; Partners and Referral lead quality

Partners produced the fastest revenue growth (**77.1%**) while improving activation by **5.3 points**. Referral revenue rose **56.2%** with a **5.1-point** activation gain. Paid Search moved in the opposite direction: signups rose **47.2%**, but revenue fell **18.3%**. That divergence makes Paid Search the highest-priority diagnostic, not the highest-priority scaling channel.

### Read the channel scorecard

Use the exact values below to compare scale and quality together. Positive signup growth is only attractive when activation, paid conversion, and revenue also remain healthy.

## Recommended Next Steps

1. **Diagnose Paid Search before adding budget.** Split performance by campaign, keyword, landing page, device, and geography; inspect whether the May decline is concentrated.
2. **Run controlled scaling tests for Partners and Referral.** Increase exposure in small steps and monitor activation, paid conversion, revenue per signup, and support intensity.
3. **Protect Organic quality.** Organic remains the largest healthy source; monitor it as the baseline while other channels change.
4. **Add guardrails.** Pair signup targets with activation rate and tickets per 100 signups so volume cannot mask deteriorating acquisition quality.

## Further Questions

- Did Paid Search mix shift toward a new campaign, keyword group, device, or geography?
- Are support tickets concentrated in onboarding, billing, or product defects?
- Do Partners and Referral retain their advantage after 30- or 60-day retention is added?
- What is customer acquisition cost by channel, and does it change the scaling recommendation?

## Explore the Underlying Rows

This preview exposes the dataset grain used by the SQL: one acquisition channel per complete week. Open the source controls on cards, charts, and tables to inspect definitions and queries.

## Caveats and Assumptions

- The dataset is synthetic and demonstrates workflow mechanics rather than a real company result.
- There are only eight complete weeks, so findings are descriptive and not causal.
- Acquisition cost, retention, campaign mix, and ticket categories are absent; each could change the recommended allocation.
- Rates use signups as the denominator, and no rows are excluded.
